business_problem: Repsol wanted to give employees more autonomy to build the apps and automations they needed, instead of relying only on centralized IT teams and spreadsheet-based or paper-based processes.
solution_summary: Repsol opened Microsoft Power Platform to its workforce through a governed DIY program that turns citizen development into a reusable operating model. Power Apps and Power Automate are used by departments to replace spreadsheet-based and paper-based processes, while Power BI tracks app adoption and user progress and Microsoft Teams hosts the SOS DIY support community. The Center of Excellence built with Kabel and Avanade provides governance, standards, and adoption support so local teams can create solutions without fragmenting the environment. Examples range from service-station training apps to fuel-movement applications that track truck flows, liters provisioned, and product status for mining operations. By combining low-code development with centralized reporting and peer support, Repsol created a scalable system for internal automation that extends IT self-service across hundreds of departments while keeping visibility into what is being built and how it performs.

solution_components.name: Power Apps
solution_components.role: Lets employees and departments build low-code applications that digitize operational work.

solution_components.name: Power Automate
solution_components.role: Automates repeatable process steps within the DIY program’s local solutions.

solution_components.name: Power BI
solution_components.role: Tracks app adoption, user progress, and the impact of citizen-development activity.

solution_components.name: Microsoft Teams
solution_components.role: Hosts the SOS DIY support community where users share projects and advice.

data_flow: Departmental needs are turned into Power Apps and Power Automate workflows, adoption and progress metrics are tracked in Power BI, and knowledge about those solutions is shared through the Teams-based SOS DIY community.
business_outcome: Repsol has built a large citizen-developer community, reduced manual work, and realized multimillion-euro savings while giving departments faster paths to their own operational tools.

evidence_quotes: The program aims to extend the reach of low-code solutions – particularly Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI – across Repsol’s departments.
With more than 486 apps already active, Repsol’s DIY program is fast gaining traction across hundreds of departments around the world.
We’ve estimated savings of about €5 million between 2022 and 2023.
